classification.difficultyReason: Recognise reciprocal quantities as common unknown expressions, reduce a three-equation system by staged elimination, then invert and check the original non-linear-looking equations.

answer.short:
$x=\frac15,\ y=1,\ z=-\frac14$.

Set $u=\frac{1}{x}$, $v=\frac{1}{y}$ and $w=\frac{1}{z}$, then eliminate.
answer.worked:
Let $u=\frac1x$, $v=\frac1y$ and $w=\frac1z$.
$$\begin{aligned}u-v&=4 &&(1)\\v-w&=5 &&(2)\\u+w&=1 &&(3)\end{aligned}$$
$(1)+(2)$:
$$\begin{align*}(u-v)+(v-w)&=4+5\\u-w&=9\end{align*}$$
Add this equation to (3):
$$\begin{align*}(u-w)+(u+w)&=9+1\\2u&=10\\u&=5\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}5-v&=4\\v&=1\\5+w&=1\\w&=-4\end{align*}$$
Hence $x=\frac15$, $y=1$ and $z=-\frac14$.
Check: $5-1=4$, $1-(-4)=5$ and $5+(-4)=1$.

answer.short:
$x=\frac15,\ y=\frac32,\ z=2$.

Set $u=\frac{1}{x}$ and $v=\frac{1}{y}$, then eliminate $z$.
answer.worked:
Let $u=\frac1x$ and $v=\frac1y$.
$$\begin{aligned}2u-3v+4z&=16 &&(1)\\u+6v-z&=7 &&(2)\\3u-v+\frac z3&=15 &&(3)\end{aligned}$$
$(1)+4(2)$:
$$\begin{align*}(2u-3v+4z)+4(u+6v-z)&=16+28\\6u+21v&=44 &&(4)\end{align*}$$
$3(3)+(2)$:
$$\begin{align*}3(3u-v+\tfrac z3)+(u+6v-z)&=45+7\\10u+3v&=52 &&(5)\end{align*}$$
$7(5)-(4)$:
$$\begin{align*}7(10u+3v)-(6u+21v)&=364-44\\64u&=320\\u&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (5):
$$\begin{align*}10(5)+3v&=52\\3v&=2\\v&=\frac23\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}5+6\left(\frac23\right)-z&=7\\9-z&=7\\z&=2\end{align*}$$
Hence $x=\frac15$, $y=\frac32$ and $z=2$.
Check: $10-2+8=16$, $5+4-2=7$ and $15-\frac23+\frac23=15$.
